data.title: Serverless
data.tagline: Run backend code on demand without managing a long-running server
data.description: A serverless function is deployed to a managed platform and starts when an HTTP request, schedule, or event triggers it. It reduces server operations for small independent tasks, but runtime limits, cold starts, regions, and stateless execution still shape the design.

avoid: Keep important state only in function memory
Run a long job beyond the platform limit
Assume there is no infrastructure or cost to manage
Split a simple workflow into too many tiny functions

lessonPractice.title: A small site only needs a contact form that saves submissions and sends notifications, without server maintenance. Which approach fits?

options.label: Use a short serverless function, persist data externally, and configure timeouts and secrets
options.feedback: The task is brief and request-driven, so the platform can manage runtime while persistence and secrets use appropriate services.

options.label: Store form submissions in function memory and read them from later requests
options.feedback: Requests may reach different instances and instances disappear, so function memory is not durable storage.

options.label: Keep one invocation running for hours and use it for video transcoding too
options.feedback: Short functions have duration and resource limits; long jobs require suitable queues or compute services.

data.agentPrompt: Handle the contact form with a short stateless serverless function that validates input, writes to external storage, and sends a notification. Keep secrets in platform environment variables and handle duplicates, timeouts, and retries without relying on function memory.
